skill.name: planning-sprints
skill.description: Plans software sprints by defining goals, prioritizing backlogs, estimating capacity, reviewing velocity, identifying dependencies, and documenting scope with an included template.
skill.summary: Create capacity-aware sprint plans from backlog priorities, team availability, and historical velocity.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: All 59 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and ordinary sprint terminology. The reviewed files contain no Ruby backtick execution or reconnaissance behavior. A medium semantic risk remains because automatic delegation can trigger state-changing GitHub operations without a clear confirmation checkpoint.

remediation.issue: State-changing GitHub operations can occur through automatic delegation without explicit confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before creating boards, changing labels, reordering backlogs, or writing sprint files. Keep discovery commands read-only by default.

content.value_statement: Teams often overcommit because backlog priority, capacity, and dependencies are considered separately. This skill combines them into a structured sprint plan with measurable goals.
actual_capabilities: Applies RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, and value-versus-effort methods to backlog items.
Calculates practical sprint capacity from team size, working days, availability, leave, and meetings.
Uses recent completed sprints to estimate velocity and recommend a buffered commitment.
Defines a focused sprint goal, success criteria, prioritized scope, dependencies, risks, and completion standards.
Structures sprint reviews, retrospectives, progress checks, burndown analysis, and follow-up actions.
Produces sprint plan documents using the included Markdown template.
limitations: Only the sprint plan template is included; referenced calculators, backlog templates, and guidance files are absent.
GitHub data requires an authenticated gh CLI and repository access.
Estimates depend on accurate backlog details, historical velocity, and team availability.
The skill cannot guarantee delivery or replace team agreement on scope and estimates.

use_cases.title: Plan the next product sprint
use_cases.description: Turn a prioritized backlog and product objective into a focused sprint goal, balanced scope, and clear success criteria.

use_cases.title: Set a realistic team commitment
use_cases.description: Combine recent velocity, leave, meetings, and team changes to recommend a sustainable sprint commitment.

use_cases.title: Recover a sprint at risk
use_cases.description: Assess burndown, blockers, and remaining scope, then prepare options for descoping or unblocking work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic sprint plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a two-week sprint plan for [team] using this backlog: [items]. Team capacity is [availability], and recent velocity is [points].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the backlog, capacity, and velocity are already known.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize [backlog items] using [RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, or value versus effort]. Explain each score, dependency, risk, and recommended sprint order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before planning when backlog order is unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Review sprint health
prompt_templates.prompt: Review sprint [name] at day [number] using completed, active, blocked, and remaining work. Identify delivery risk and recommend specific scope changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use during a sprint when progress differs from the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare advanced scope options
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a sprint plan from [backlog], [velocity history], [availability], and [strategic goals]. Compare two scope options, test dependencies, and define measurable success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex planning with competing objectives and uncertain dependencies.

output_examples.input: Plan a two-week authentication sprint for four engineers with a recent velocity of 34 points.
output_examples.output: Goal: Release secure sign-in and password recovery. Commitment: 30 points with a four-point buffer. Risks: API review and security testing dependencies.

output_examples.input: Prioritize six backlog items using RICE scores and dependencies.
output_examples.output: First: login reliability because it has high reach and blocks onboarding. Next: password recovery and session controls. Defer cosmetic profile changes.

output_examples.input: Review a sprint with 16 points remaining after seven of ten days.
output_examples.output: Status: At risk. Recommended action: move the lowest-value five-point item and escalate the blocking API review today. Preserve the primary sprint goal.

best_practices: Provide current backlog details, recent velocity, team availability, and sprint dates before requesting a plan.
Validate estimates and dependencies with the delivery team before committing the sprint.
Reserve capacity for uncertainty and update the plan when approved scope changes occur.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated priorities as final without product and engineering review.
Do not compare velocity across teams because story-point scales differ.
Do not allow automatic board, label, or file changes without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Which planning methods does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, value-versus-effort analysis, velocity review, and capacity planning.

faq.question: Can it read my GitHub backlog?
faq.answer: Yes, when the gh CLI is authenticated and repository access is available. Review repository scope before running commands.

faq.question: Does it create or update GitHub boards?
faq.answer: The instructions can delegate GitHub operations to another skill. Require confirmation before any board, label, or backlog change.

faq.question: How much capacity should a sprint use?
faq.answer: The guidance recommends approximately 80 to 90 percent of calculated capacity, with room for uncertainty and urgent work.

faq.question: Are the referenced planning scripts included?
faq.answer: No. This package contains the main skill file and one sprint plan template, but the referenced calculator scripts are absent.

faq.question: Can this skill guarantee sprint delivery?
faq.answer: No. It structures planning decisions, but delivery still depends on estimates, dependencies, team availability, and changing conditions.
